concepts.def: If an electrical conductor moves relative to a magnetic field, or if there is a change in the magnetic field around a conductor, a potential difference is induced across the ends of the conductor. If the conductor is part of a complete circuit, a current is induced in the conductor. This is called the generator effect.

The potential difference that appears across the ends of a conductor because of relative movement between the conductor and a magnetic field, or because of a change in the magnetic field around it. No cell is needed. A current is induced only if the conductor forms part of a complete circuit.

An induced current generates a magnetic field that opposes the original change, either the movement of the conductor or the change in magnetic field. This is why a force must be applied, and work done, to keep a generator turning or to push a magnet into a coil.

concepts.term: Factors affecting the size of the induced potential difference
concepts.def: The size of the induced potential difference or induced current is increased by moving the conductor or magnet faster, by using a stronger magnetic field, and by using a coil with more turns. In short, the faster the magnetic field through the coil changes, the larger the induced potential difference.

concepts.term: Factors affecting the direction of the induced potential difference
concepts.def: The direction of the induced potential difference or induced current is reversed by reversing the direction of the movement, or by reversing the poles of the magnet, that is by reversing the direction of the magnetic field. Changing the speed or the number of turns alters only the size.

A generator that uses the generator effect to produce alternating current. A coil rotates in a magnetic field and is connected to the external circuit through slip rings, so each end of the coil stays joined to the same contact and the induced potential difference reverses every half turn.

A generator that uses the generator effect to produce direct current. A coil rotates in a magnetic field and is connected to the external circuit through a split-ring commutator, so the connections swap every half turn and the output potential difference never reverses.

The two continuous metal rings, one joined to each end of the rotating coil of an alternator, that keep each end of the coil connected to the same brush all the time. Because the connections never swap, the output alternates in direction as the coil turns.

The divided metal ring used in a dynamo. Every half turn each half of the ring meets the other brush, so the connections to the external circuit swap over at the moment the induced potential difference would otherwise reverse. The output therefore stays in one direction.

concepts.term: Potential difference against time graph for a generator
concepts.def: For an alternator the graph is a wave that rises and falls equally above and below the time axis, reversing every half turn. For a dynamo the graph is a series of humps all on the same side of the axis. Turning the coil faster makes the peaks both taller and closer together.

A device that uses the generator effect to convert the pressure variations in sound waves into variations in current in electrical circuits. The pressure variations make a diaphragm vibrate, the diaphragm moves a coil over a magnet, and the movement of the coil in the magnetic field induces a potential difference that varies in step with the sound wave.

A basic transformer consists of a primary coil and a secondary coil wound on an iron core. An alternating current in the primary coil produces a continually changing magnetic field in the core; that changing field passes through the secondary coil and induces an alternating potential difference across it. The two coils are not joined electrically.

The core on which the primary and secondary coils of a basic transformer are wound. Iron is used as it is easily magnetised, so it carries the changing magnetic field from the primary coil through to the secondary coil.

The ratio of the potential differences across the primary and secondary coils of a transformer Vp and Vs depends on the ratio of the number of turns on each coil, np and ns: Vp / Vs = np / ns, with potential difference, Vp and Vs in volts, V.

A transformer with more turns on the secondary coil than on the primary coil, so that in a step-up transformer Vs > Vp. Because the power output cannot exceed the power input, the secondary current is smaller than the primary current.

A transformer with fewer turns on the secondary coil than on the primary coil, so that in a step-down transformer Vs < Vp. Because the power output cannot exceed the power input, the secondary current is larger than the primary current.

If transformers were 100% efficient, the electrical power output would equal the electrical power input: Vs × Is = Vp × Ip, where Vs × Is is the power output (secondary coil) and Vp × Ip is the power input (primary coil), with power input and output, in watts, W.

The unit of potential difference. In the transformer equation the potential difference, Vp and Vs, is in volts, V. A transformer changes the size of a potential difference; it does not change the unit it is measured in.
The unit of power. In the transformer power equation the power input and output, in watts, W, are each found by multiplying a potential difference in volts by a current in amperes.

Power is transmitted across the National Grid at a very high potential difference. For a given power transfer, Vp × Ip is fixed, so raising the potential difference lowers the current in the transmission cables. A smaller current wastes less energy heating the cables, which is the advantage of power transmission at high potential differences.

mcqs.q: A straight copper rod lies horizontally between the poles of a strong magnet. Which action induces a potential difference across the ends of the rod?
options: Moving the rod steadily downwards through the magnetic field
Holding the rod still between the poles of a strong magnet
Joining the ends of the rod with a length of copper wire
Warming the rod so that its resistance rises a little
mcqs.explain: The conductor moves relative to the magnetic field, so a potential difference is induced across the ends of the rod.

mcqs.q: A wire is moved through a magnetic field. The two ends of the wire are not connected to anything at all. What is induced in the wire?
options: Nothing at all, because the circuit around it is incomplete
A current, but no potential difference across the ends
A potential difference, but no current flows in the wire
Both a potential difference and a current in the wire
mcqs.explain: A potential difference is induced across the ends of the conductor; a current is induced only if the conductor is part of a complete circuit.

mcqs.q: The north pole of a magnet is pushed towards a coil that is part of a complete circuit. What does the magnetic field produced by the induced current do?
options: It reinforces the change, pulling the magnet deeper into the coil
It opposes the change, so it acts to repel the approaching pole
It strengthens the magnet's own field inside the coil, reinforcing it
It acts only on the coil itself and never on the magnet
mcqs.explain: An induced current generates a magnetic field that opposes the original change, here the movement of the magnet towards the coil.

mcqs.q: A student pushes a magnet into a coil that is part of a complete circuit. Why must the student do work to keep the magnet moving inwards?
options: The induced magnetic field attracts the magnet, so it must be held back
Friction in the coil's windings resists the magnet as it moves in
The copper wire has resistance, so pushing charge along it takes force
An induced magnetic field pushes back on the moving magnet
mcqs.explain: The induced current generates a magnetic field that opposes the movement of the magnet, so a force is needed to keep it moving.

mcqs.q: A coil is rotated between the poles of a magnet. Which change would increase the size of the potential difference induced in the coil?
options: Using thicker copper wire of lower resistance for the coil
Winding more turns onto the coil and then rotating it faster
Holding the coil still in the strongest part of the field
Rotating a coil that has far fewer turns of wire on it
mcqs.explain: More turns and a faster rate of change of the magnetic field both increase the size of the induced potential difference.

mcqs.q: A north pole is pushed into a coil and the meter needle flicks to the right. Which change would make the needle flick to the left instead?
options: Pushing the same north pole in far more quickly than before
Winding many more turns of wire onto the same coil
Pushing a much stronger north pole in at the same speed
Pulling the same north pole straight back out of the coil
mcqs.explain: Reversing the direction of the relative movement reverses the direction of the induced potential difference and current.

mcqs.q: A magnet is pushed into a coil connected to an ammeter, held completely still inside the coil for two seconds, and then pulled out. What does the ammeter read while the magnet is held still?
options: Zero, because the field through the coil is not changing
A steady current, because the magnet's field is inside the coil
A reversed current, because stopping the magnet flips its direction
A current that grows slowly while the magnet is inside
mcqs.explain: With no relative movement and no change in the magnetic field, nothing is induced.

mcqs.q: A wire is moved downwards between the poles of a magnet, and then moved upwards at twice the speed. Compared with the downward movement, the potential difference induced during the upward movement is:
options: twice the size, in the same direction as before
the same size, but in the opposite direction
twice the size, in the opposite direction
the same size and the same direction as before
mcqs.explain: Doubling the speed doubles the size, and reversing the direction of movement reverses the direction of the induced potential difference.

mcqs.q: An alternator and a dynamo are both turned steadily by the same motor. How do their outputs differ?
options: The dynamo generates ac and the alternator generates dc
Both generate ac, though the dynamo's output is larger
The alternator generates ac, while the dynamo generates dc
The alternator uses the motor effect, not induction
mcqs.explain: The generator effect is used in an alternator to generate ac and in a dynamo to generate dc.

mcqs.q: A dynamo and an alternator have identical coils and magnets. Which part of the dynamo makes its output a direct current?
options: A split-ring commutator, which swaps the connections every half turn
A pair of slip rings, which keep the coil joined to the same contacts
A commutator that holds the output at one steady value
An iron core that stores the current between the half turns
mcqs.explain: Swapping the connections each half turn keeps the output potential difference in one direction.

mcqs.q: Which describes the graph of potential difference generated in the coil against time for a dynamo turning steadily?
options: A straight horizontal line at one constant positive value
A wave that rises and falls equally either side of the axis
A flat line held at a constant value below the axis
A series of humps that never cross below the time axis
mcqs.explain: The dynamo's output rises and falls as the coil turns but never reverses direction.

mcqs.q: The coil of an alternator is turned twice as fast as before. How does the graph of potential difference against time change?
options: Just as tall as before, but the peaks are spaced further apart
The peaks are taller and closer together
The peaks are closer but no taller than before
The trace no longer dips below the axis, staying all positive
mcqs.explain: A faster rotation changes the field through the coil faster, giving a larger induced potential difference more often.

mcqs.q: How does a microphone make use of the generator effect?
options: Variations in current are converted into pressure variations in the air
Sound shakes the magnet to and fro inside a coil that stays fixed
Sound waves are absorbed by a magnet, which then makes a current
Pressure variations in a sound wave are converted into variations in current
mcqs.explain: Microphones use the generator effect to convert the pressure variations in sound waves into variations in current in electrical circuits.

mcqs.q: A sound wave reaches the diaphragm of a moving-coil microphone. What happens next?
options: The diaphragm makes the magnet vibrate inside a coil that is fixed
The diaphragm and its coil vibrate near a magnet, inducing a current
A current in the coil makes the diaphragm vibrate and give out a sound
The magnet swings to and fro past a coil clamped firmly in place
mcqs.explain: The coil moving in the magnetic field induces a potential difference that varies in step with the pressure variations.

mcqs.q: What does a basic transformer consist of?
options: A primary coil and a secondary coil joined by a copper wire
Two coils wound on a solid copper core so charge passes easily across
A primary coil and a secondary coil wound on an iron core
A primary and secondary coil linked through the iron core carrying the current
mcqs.explain: This is exactly the construction given in the specification.

mcqs.q: Why is the core of a basic transformer made of iron?
options: Iron is easily magnetised by the changing field
Iron conducts an electric current better than copper
Iron carries the current across from one coil to the other
Iron does not get hot when a current flows in it
mcqs.explain: Iron is used as it is easily magnetised, so it carries the changing field to the secondary coil.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly links the potential differences and the numbers of turns on the two coils of a transformer?
options: Vp / Vs = np / ns, so the ratio of the pds equals the ratio of the turns
Vp / Vs = ns / np, so the ratio of the pds is the inverse turns ratio
Vp + Vs = np + ns, so the pds and the turns must add up to match
Ip = Is, so the current is the same in both coils whatever the turns
mcqs.explain: This is the equation as the specification states it, with potential difference, Vp and Vs in volts, V.

mcqs.q: A transformer has 40 turns on its primary coil and 800 turns on its secondary coil. The potential difference across the primary coil is 15 V. What is the potential difference across the secondary coil?
options: 300 watts
mcqs.explain: Vp / Vs = np / ns, so Vs = 15 × 800 / 40 = 300 V, a step-up transformer with Vs > Vp.

mcqs.q: A transformer has 1200 turns on its primary coil, 60 turns on its secondary coil, and a primary potential difference of 240 V. Which describes this transformer and its secondary potential difference?
options: Step-up, and the secondary potential difference becomes 4800 V
Step-down, and the secondary pd is only 0.2 V
Step-down, and the secondary potential difference is 12 V
Step-up, so the secondary current is 20 times larger
mcqs.explain: Fewer turns on the secondary gives Vs < Vp: Vs = 240 × 60 / 1200 = 12 V.

mcqs.q: Which units belong with the quantities in the transformer equations?
options: Potential difference in watts, W; and power in volts, V
Potential difference in volts, V; power in watts, W
Potential difference in watts, W; power in amperes, A
Potential difference in watts, W; power in joules, J
mcqs.explain: Potential difference, Vp and Vs in volts, V; power input and output, in watts, W.

mcqs.q: A transformer is described as 100% efficient. What does this tell you about its coils?
options: The current in the secondary coil equals the current in the primary coil
The secondary coil delivers more power than the primary takes in
The power output at the secondary equals the power input at the primary
The current passes straight from the primary coil into the secondary
mcqs.explain: If transformers were 100% efficient, the electrical power output would equal the electrical power input: Vs × Is = Vp × Ip.

mcqs.q: A transformer that can be treated as 100% efficient supplies 24 W to a lamp from a 230 V mains supply. What current is drawn from the input supply?
mcqs.explain: Vp × Ip equals the power output, so Ip = 24 / 230 = 0.104 A.

mcqs.q: Why is electrical power transmitted across the National Grid at a very high potential difference?
options: A high pd means a small current, so less energy heats the cables
A high pd lowers the resistance of the cables, so less energy is wasted
A high pd drives a large current, which carries the power to homes faster
A high pd increases the power delivered to each of the homes
mcqs.explain: For a fixed power transfer Vp × Ip is fixed, so a higher potential difference gives a smaller current and less heating of the cables.

mcqs.q: Why must the supply connected to the primary coil of a transformer be an alternating current?
options: A direct current cannot pass along the wire of the primary coil at all
An alternating current can jump the gap between the two coils
A direct current would make the iron core melt with the heat
Only a changing current gives a changing field in the core
mcqs.explain: An alternating current keeps the magnetic field in the core changing, and only a changing field induces a potential difference in the secondary coil.

mcqs.q: A power station transformer has 500 turns on the primary and 25 000 on the secondary. The primary coil takes 8000 A at 25 kV. What is the current in the secondary coil?
mcqs.explain: Vp / Vs = np / ns gives Vs = 25 × 25 000 / 500 = 1250 kV, then Vs × Is = Vp × Ip gives Is = 25 × 8000 / 1250 = 160 A.

mcqs.q: A grid link transfers 200 MW. Transformers raise the transmission potential difference from 25 kV to 400 kV. What is the current in the cables now?
mcqs.explain: Power = pd × current, so I = 200 000 000 / 400 000 = 500 A: sixteen times smaller, so far less energy heats the cables.
